brief: Goldman Sachs summarises Day 2 of its Communacopia + Technology Conference, where TSMC, Amkor, NXP, Cadence, SanDisk, IBM, Teradyne, Applied Materials and SiTime presented. The chain the note draws: agentic AI broadens compute demand beyond accelerators into CPUs, networking and DRAM, so leading-edge wafer, advanced packaging, memory and test capacity all stay tight, so vendors extend capacity on multi-year customer visibility. TSMC says N3 supply is still insufficient, CoWoS is tight enough that it now outsources some packaging to OSATs, and power and memory are the bottlenecks others cite. Applied Materials reiterates roughly 40% 2026 revenue growth, Amkor its $11bn 2030 target, SanDisk that NAND tightness runs through 2027 and possibly 2028. TSMC's Arizona Phase 1 reaches Taiwan-comparable yields and profitability, which it uses to argue geographic flexibility is worth a pricing premium, while N2 ramp and overseas dilution of 2 to 3 percentage points each still leave its 56%-and-above gross margin target intact. Analog names describe recovering end demand without broad OEM restocking. Goldman restates Buy ratings and 12-month price targets on every name except Amkor, rated Neutral.
